cognate: ON stela/stelask ~ Ved. tsar- 'creep up stealthily' (*tsel-; equation not universally accepted); ON sofandi ~ Ved. svapant- (*swep-, present participle)
drift_or_renewal: Germanic *stelan- otherwise 'steal'; here the mediopassive keeps the older 'sneak (up on)' sense that Vedic tsar- has
shared_syntax: verb of stealthy approach + accusative victim + predicative present participle 'sleeping' (ON stelask á X sofanda; Ved. tvā svapantīṃ tsarati); both contexts add the waking counterpart (Ved. jāgratīm; ON next unit hefði vakat)
context: hostile stealthy attack on a sleeping victim: AV charm against demons who creep on a woman asleep or awake; Þiðreks saga reproach for killing Ekka's brother in his sleep

cognate: Ved. sū́rya- ~ Gk ἥλιος (*sóh₂wl̥); Ved. uṣás- ~ Gk ἠώς (*h₂éwsōs); Ved. jajā́na/janáyan ~ Gk γείνατο (*ǵenh₁-)
drift_or_renewal: none (Greek also uses the pair as a direction formula, πρὸς ἠῶ τ’ ἠέλιόν τε 'eastward')
shared_syntax: coordinated binomial of the two cosmic nouns as objects (Ved. asyndetic sū́ryam uṣásam, recurrent as a fixed pair; Gk ἠῶ τ’ ἠέλιόν τε, formulaic); in cosmogony both pairs are objects of *ǵenh₁- (Indra jajā́na sū́ryam uṣásam; Theia Ἠέλιον ... Ἠῶ γείνατο)
context: cosmogony/divine genealogy in RV 1.32, 2.12, 3.32 and Hes. Th. 371-374; the Iliad anchor uses the same binomial as a world-merism ('all horses under dawn and sun')

cognate: ON gull ~ Russ. золото (*ǵʰl̥h₃tó- / *ǵʰolh₃to-); ON rauðr, OE rēad, MW rhudd (in rhuddaur) from *h₁rewdʰ-
drift_or_renewal: Russian renews 'red' with красный (also 'fine, beautiful'; cf. червонное золото); Old Irish renews with derg (dergór); Welsh rhuddaur keeps the *h₁rewdʰ- adjective with the Latin loan aur
shared_syntax: attributive colour adjective 'red' + 'gold' as a material genitive/attribute of precious objects (ON af/með rauðu gulli; Russ. рубашки красна золота)
context: description of costly gilded war-gear or garments in heroic narrative (Þiðreks saga shield; bylina shirts of red gold)

near_miss.lead: night + darkness *mergʷ- (ON nótt ... myrkr/myrkast; Serb. ноћ ... мрак, мркла ноћ)
near_miss.why_not: *mergʷ- is a Germanic-Balto-Slavic word; search finds the pair only in ON prose and Vuk; 'darkness of night' is generic; the Edda formula with myrkr is myrkvan við, not night

near_miss.lead: 'midnight' *médʰyā nókʷts (ON um miðja nátt / mið nótt, Lat. media nocte, Gk μέσαι νύκτες)
near_miss.why_not: an inherited adjective-of-position construction, but the phrase is transparent and re-formed everywhere; no shared context beyond time-reckoning

near_miss.lead: 'dark night' (Russ. темную ночь, Lith. tamsi naktelė, OHG finstar naht, all *temH- + *nókʷts) / spending the night asleep vs Gk ἀΰπνους νύκτας ἴαυον
near_miss.why_not: *temH- + night found in byliny, dainos and OHG only (late or Christian texts), and 'dark night' is too generic to argue inheritance; Homer has sleepless nights with no cognate figure
shared roots nókʷts and *swep- only; no shared wording

near_miss.lead: ON áðr en sól væri í austri ~ Gk πρὸς ἠῶ τ’ ἠέλιόν τε 'east'
near_miss.why_not: ON 'sun in the east' is a legal/time-of-day mark (also in law codes); naming east by sunrise is universal; only the Ved.-Gk binomial is claimed

near_miss.lead: serpent on the weapon (ON ormr renni on the blade; Gk κυάνεος δράκων on Agamemnon's baldric)
near_miss.why_not: motif, not wording: ON ormr (*wr̥mis) and Gk δράκων are not cognate; the Russian partner (сизой орёл) is unrelated

near_miss.lead: heart burns and glows like gold glows (ON glóa ... gull)
near_miss.why_not: no partner wording; the Middle Irish passage is about form without sense
